# UI — visual direction, tokens, routes

## Direction

Light, editorial product app. Warm white ground, navy for every primary action,
gold reserved for the brand mark and "filed/complete" status — never a general
accent or button color. The reference points are Linear and Superhuman for
density and keyboard-forward habits; the surface treatment itself reads closer
to a well-made financial-services document than a SaaS dashboard.

**This supersedes an earlier dark-theme direction.** The product shipped as a
near-black UI through P0–P2, then moved to this light theme deliberately across
several commits in August 2026 ("Change page background from warm beige to
white", "Polish light theme", "Add a pronounced floating shadow to all cards",
"Round out corners for a softer, less boxy feel"). Light is the only theme now —
the same "do not build a second theme without asking" rule applies, just to the
opposite polarity.

Optimised equally for two contexts: an associate logging on a phone between
calls, and an SMD scanning a roster on a laptop. Both get the same visual system.

What produces the look, in order of impact:

1. **Pure white ground, one step of tint for interaction feedback.** `#FFFFFF`
   canvas and panels; `#F4F4F5` for hover states and sunken surfaces (row hover,
   input backgrounds). There is no separate "raised panel" tone the way the old
   dark system had three ground steps — on white, elevation comes from shadow
   and border, not from a lighter fill.
2. **Borders are a warm hairline, not pure grey.** `#E7E2D3` at full opacity for
   the base line; two escalating steps derived from the text-1 navy at low alpha
   (`rgba(20,33,61,.14)`, `rgba(20,33,61,.22)`) for stronger emphasis (active
   tab-group container, focus-adjacent dividers).
3. **Text never hits pure black.** `#14213D` (a navy-black) is the ceiling —
   consistent with the accent family below, so text and primary actions read as
   one family of ink rather than two unrelated colors.
4. **One accent, used sparingly: navy.** `#0B1E3D` for primary buttons, active
   nav, selected state, links, and the activity matrix. Never gold for any of
   these — gold is reserved for the brand mark and "filed" status chips only.
   Mixing the two would make gold read as "another action color" and dilute the
   one place it's supposed to mean something specific.
5. **Cards float, deliberately more than a typical flat UI.** A two-tier shadow
   system: `lift` (`0 1px 3px rgba(11,30,61,.10), 0 1px 2px rgba(11,30,61,.08)`)
   for buttons, inputs, and small controls; `card` (`0 14px 32px -8px
   rgba(11,30,61,.20), 0 4px 12px -2px rgba(11,30,61,.12)`) for every `Card` and
   card-style surface — KPI tiles, the Next Up card, list/table containers.
   `float` sits between the two for popovers, dropdowns, toasts, and the mobile
   tab bar. This is heavier than a typical dense-data-app default; it was a
   deliberate request, not an accident — the payoff is that cards read as
   physically separate objects on the page rather than boxes drawn with a
   border.
6. **Tight type, Plus Jakarta Sans instead of a system stack.** 13px base body
   (`sm`), `-.006em` tracking, `-.025em` on headings, weights capped at 700 for
   headings / 600 elsewhere. Numbers in JetBrains Mono at weight 500 with heavy
   negative tracking (`-.045em`) — thin and wide, not chunky. The type scale
   runs `xs 12 / sm 13 / base 14 / lg 16 / xl 18 / 2xl 20 / 3xl 24`, all with
   generous line-heights (1.5–1.8) — a document-like reading rhythm rather than
   a tight app-UI rhythm.
7. **Soft, generous radii.** `10px` small controls, `14px` cards and the default
   scale, `20px` for larger surfaces, `28px` reserved for buttons specifically
   (see `size:lg` in `button.tsx`) so buttons read a step softer than the
   containers around them. This is a deliberate step up from a typical dense-app
   radius scale (6–12px) for a warmer, less boxy feel — confirmed by the
   "Round out corners" commit.

## Tokens

```css
:root {
  /* ground */
  --bg: #FFFFFF; --panel: #FFFFFF; --hover: #F4F4F5; --sunken: #F4F4F5;
  /* hairlines */
  --line: #E7E2D3;
  --line-2: rgba(20, 33, 61, 0.14); --line-3: rgba(20, 33, 61, 0.22);
  /* text */
  --fg: #14213D; --fg-2: #5C6580; --fg-3: #94A0B8;
  --fg-4: rgba(148, 160, 184, 0.7); /* derived, no dedicated spec token */
  /* accent — primary actions, never gold */
  --acc: #0B1E3D; --acc-2: #122A54;
  --acc-dim: rgba(11, 30, 61, 0.07); --acc-line: rgba(11, 30, 61, 0.28);
  /* brand mark + "filed"/complete status ONLY */
  --gold: #C9A227; --gold-dark: #9C7C1A; --gold-light: #FBF3D9;
  /* attainment only */
  --ok: #1B7A43; --ok-dim: #E4F5EA;
  --warn: #9C6A0A; --warn-dim: #FBF0DA;
  --bad: #B0392A; --bad-dim: #FBE6E2;
  /* form */
  --r-sm: 10px; --r: 14px; --r-lg: 20px; --r-xl: 28px; /* buttons only */
  --lift: 0 1px 3px rgba(11,30,61,.10), 0 1px 2px -1px rgba(11,30,61,.08);
  --float: 0 8px 24px -4px rgba(11,30,61,.16), 0 2px 8px -2px rgba(11,30,61,.10);
  --card: 0 14px 32px -8px rgba(11,30,61,.20), 0 4px 12px -2px rgba(11,30,61,.12);
  --ui: 'Plus Jakarta Sans', -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', sans-serif;
  --mono: 'JetBrains Mono', ui-monospace, monospace;
}
```

Source of truth for these values is `tailwind.config.ts` (Tailwind color/shadow/
radius scale, with each color kept as a literal hex rather than `var()` so
Tailwind's opacity modifiers like `bg-ok/15` keep working) and `globals.css`
`:root` (the same values as CSS custom properties for anything outside
Tailwind's reach). If the two ever disagree, `tailwind.config.ts` wins — it's
what actually renders.

**Light is the only theme.** Do not build a dark mode or a theme toggle without
asking; if it's ever needed, the token layer above makes it additive the same
way it would have for the original dark system.

**Green, amber, and red mean target attainment and nothing else** — ≥100%,
70–99%, <70%. A call-outcome badge uses neutral or accent tints. Colouring
"Voicemail" red makes the roster unscannable and implies a failure that isn't one.

**The activity matrix is the signature element.** Cells that hit the daily
minimum are solid navy accent with a soft shadow glow; partial days are accent
at low alpha with muted text; zero days sink to `--sunken` with a hairline
border; future days are a dashed outline (see `daily-grid.tsx`). On this ground
the gaps are what the eye lands on first, which is exactly the finding an SMD
needs. Do not flatten this into a plain table.

## Accessibility on light

- Body text `--fg` (#14213D) on `--panel` (#FFFFFF) clears AA comfortably;
  `--fg-3` is for non-essential secondary text only — never for a value a user
  must read.
- Focus ring is a two-layer effect: `outline: 2px solid var(--surface)` +
  `box-shadow: 0 0 0 4px var(--navy)` so it reads on any surface without
  fighting the card shadow system. Never remove the outline without replacing
  it (see `*:focus-visible` in `globals.css`).
- Touch targets ≥44px on mobile — enforced at the primitive level
  (`min-h-[44px]` on the base `Button` class) even where the visual control
  looks smaller (`size="sm"` renders at a visual 36px height but the browser's
  `min-height` still constrains the actual hit target to 44px).
- Honour `prefers-reduced-motion` — implemented globally in `globals.css`.
- Charts carry an `sr-only` data-table fallback with a `<caption>` (see
  `donut-chart.tsx` and siblings in `src/components/charts/`) — keep this
  pattern for any new chart type.

## Component library
shadcn/ui (Avatar, Badge, Button, Card, Checkbox, Dialog, Dropdown Menu, Input,
Label, Select, Separator, Skeleton, Sonner/Toast, Tabs, Textarea), restyled
against the tokens above. shadcn ships light-first, which made this theme
switch cheaper than the original dark restyle — but still restyle each new
component against the tokens as you add it rather than assuming defaults match.

Two deliberate simplifications from the original spec, both kept on purpose:
- **Date ranges use native `<input type="date">`**, not a Popover+Calendar
  component. More accessible and better on mobile than a custom calendar
  widget; add Popover+Calendar only if a real range-picking need (not just two
  single dates) comes up.
- **The searchable agent multi-select uses `cmdk`/Command**, as originally
  spec'd (`agent-multi-select.tsx`) — this one did ship as designed.

Charts: Recharts — line, horizontal bar, donut (`innerRadius`), and a funnel
chart for the recruiting pipeline. Grid lines and axes use `--line`; series use
`--acc` and `--acc-2`; categorical series pull from a fixed, colorblind-safe
order in `src/lib/chart-colors.ts` (Recharts fills can't consume Tailwind
classes, so this is a literal hex array kept in sync with the token palette by
hand). Add no other chart library without asking.

## Routes

Terminology, used consistently across all docs: **SMD** = the person, `leader` =
their role value, **upline** = the hierarchy relationship. They are the same
human in v1; do not invent a fourth word.

Targets live on `/team/targets`, SMD-only. One card reproducing the workbook's
gold cells (Calls Target/Wk, Appts Held Target/Wk, Premium Target/Wk, Min
Calls/Day, MD Deadline) with the same defaults 50 / 3 / $188 / 15 as the org
default, plus a per-agent override table. Saving shows an inline note that the
change applies from the coming Monday and that past weeks keep their original
target. Agents see the same card in `/settings`, read-only, with "set by your
SMD" attribution.

**Associate**
| Route | Notes |
|---|---|
| `/today` | **default landing** — the callback queue ("My Day" in nav) |
| `/logs` | unified activity list across calls/appointments/sales/recruiting (primary nav — supersedes the earlier per-type list pages as the main entry point; the per-type routes below still exist for direct CRUD/edit) |
| `/log` | quick log — now a 4-way tab switcher (Call/Appointment/Sale/Recruiting), see note below |
| `/dashboard` | week/8-week view of own numbers |
| `/contacts` | people, not call rows; drill into one contact's history |
| `/appointments`, `/sales`, `/recruiting` | list + edit, reached from `/logs` or directly |
| `/notes` | meeting notes, contact-scoped |
| `/clients` | clients derived from closed sales |
| `/import` | spreadsheet upload — contacts, or full activity logs; re-runnable, dedupes by name (phone is never collected, as of P13) |
| `/settings` | profile, read-only targets card, data export (no delete-account or import-from-settings entry points as of P13) |

**Leader** (`/team/*`, guarded by role + hierarchy)
| Route | Notes |
|---|---|
| `/team` | roster: the core screen |
| `/team/[agentId]` | aggregate drill-down, 8-week trend, funnel |
| `/team/[agentId]/daily` | day-by-day grid for one agent over a date range |
| `/team/targets` | org default + per-agent overrides |
| `/team/invites` | send/revoke invitations |
| `/team/members` | roster management, deactivation |
| `/team/organization` | org name, logo |
| `/team/audit` | audit log viewer |

**Auth, profile, settings, invitations, admin, and the navigation shell** are
specified in `docs/09-account-and-auth.md`. **Journeys and empty states** in
`docs/10-journeys.md`.

## The two screens that matter

### `/log` — quick log (mobile-first, thumb zone)

**Scope note (superseding the original spec):** the original spec described a
single bare screen for calls only, no navigation, no chrome. P3+ added three
more activity types (Appointment, Sale, Recruiting) that need their own create
forms, and rather than build four separate entry points, `/log` became a
4-way tab switcher (`log-type-switcher.tsx`) with Call as the default,
pre-selected tab. This is an intentional tradeoff: switching away from Call
costs one extra tap, but the app gains a single, discoverable "log something"
entry point instead of four. **The Call tab itself is still the fast path** —
once you're on it (the default), the five-tap flow below is unchanged.

Within the Call tab, one screen, no further navigation, no modal stack:
1. Contact name — text input, autocompletes from the agent's own prior contacts
2. Source — 6 chips, single select, last-used pre-selected
3. Outcome — 5 chips, single select
4. Save — full-width, bottom of screen, thumb-reachable

Optional (collapsed): company, notes. `Appointment Set` reveals an inline date
picker and creates the appointment row in the same submit.

Two additions that carry the whole product:
- **Call back on…** — appears on any outcome except `Not interested`, as chips:
  *Tomorrow · Monday · Next week · 1 month · Pick a date*. One tap. This field
  populates `/today` and is the reason the agent opens the app tomorrow.
- **Date chip at the top** reading *Today*, tapping opens a picker. Agents batch-log
  at 8 PM; a form that only accepts same-day entry is abandoned in week two.

Requirements: optimistic insert, toast with Undo, form resets to step 1 with
source retained, counter at top reading `7 / 15 today · 3-day streak`.
**Target: five taps, no page transition, once on the Call tab.** Offline: queue
in IndexedDB, flush on reconnect. Ship as a PWA so it installs to the home screen.

### `/team` — roster table
Dense table, one row per downline agent, default sort **% to calls goal ascending**
(worst first — this is a coaching queue, not a leaderboard):

`Agent · Calls (n/target, bar) · Appts Set · Appts Held · Premium ·
Streak · Last logged`

Show the absolute number and the target together (`37 / 50`), not a bare
percentage — the raw count is what a coaching conversation actually uses.
Agents on a per-agent override get a small marker so the SMD remembers the
denominator differs.

- Attainment-tinted mono numbers + a small horizontal bar on the Calls column
  (`attainmentColor`/`attainmentBar` in `lib/attainment.ts`); `Last logged > 7d`
  gets a muted "Quiet" badge
- Sort by any column; default sort is % to goal ascending (worst first — this is
  a coaching queue, not a leaderboard)
- Filters, the agent multi-select, the Summary/Daily/Activity view toggle, the
  team KPI strip, and the charts are all specified in `docs/08-screen-specs.md`
  — that file is authoritative for this screen's contents; this section covers
  only the table.
- Mobile: collapses to cards, name + calls bar + last-logged
- Empty state names the reason ("No one in your downline yet — invite someone")

## Rules
- Server Components render data; client components handle input only.
- Every list has loading skeleton, empty state, and error state. No spinners on
  full pages. *(Empty states are consistently implemented; per-route
  `loading.tsx`/`error.tsx` using the existing `Skeleton` primitive is tracked
  as outstanding work — see TODOS.md.)*
- Numbers right-aligned, mono, tabular-nums. Currency at the edge, never in DB.
- Dates always `Mon 11 Aug` or ISO — never `08/11`, which is ambiguous in Canada.
- Touch targets `>=44px`. Contrast AA. Every interactive element keyboard-reachable
  and labelled. Charts carry a data table fallback for screen readers.
- `⌘K` opens a command palette scoped to the agent's own contacts. Desktop only;
  it is a convenience, never the only path to anything.
- No dark-pattern gamification. Streaks are informational; do not shame.
